output.brief: VA-220 failures are coming from Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not from installers or firmware. Brenmoor's lab matched claims to unit serials: Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about the same rate (about 41 per 1,000) whether installed by legacy or new firms, and whether on firmware 4.1 or 4.2. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 in every group. Teardowns show a deformed, unseated slide seal, and 11% of unused 2026 Pellacott valves leak at the seat. Pellacott's certificates are not real test records. The only rig it had for VA-220 failed on 9 Jan 2026 and was disconnected. The other rigs have no VA-220 program. Every 2026 per-piece table repeats one of four sequences already used in Nov 2025. The score rose because it rewards submitted paperwork, so the dock-to-stock status was granted on unverified data. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and retest with Brenmoor-run helium testing. Drop the installer remediation plan. Escalate the certificate issue under the supply agreement. Check other suppliers' records for the same problem. Whether the seal change or Line 3 is the cause is not yet separated, so don't dictate the seal source yet.
